(3) Analyse every failure with evidence; a failure is acceptable only if proven not caused by this work; a test that passes and fails by turns is a defect (say so, do not rerun until green). (4) Say how long the picker spec took on the runner against the local 17 s and against 48000 ms (if it is longer than 48000 ms, say so plainly: ORCH must ask the owner). (5) Check afterwards that no sai-e2e process and no sai-e2e temporary folder of yours is left, and that the working tree is as before your step (git status --short, sha256 of .git/index, sha256 over the run's files). Compare the local and the GitHub totals with the CI limit of 30 minutes (watch value about 25 minutes) and state the margin. PASS only if both runs are green or every failure is proven not caused by this work; otherwise FAIL. Do not edit the project (only this handoff), do not commit to any branch other than the temporary ci/ branch, do not push to main. The Mac has crashed under load before: one heavy job at a time.

issues.text: The task (and AP-141, item 2) asks to run handoffs-check and traces on 'a copy outside the project made with git archive of the snapshot commit'. Taken literally this cannot be run: both commands list files through git and give exit 2 E_TRACE_NOT_GIT on a plain archive copy (shown in self_check). I gave the archive copy its own git metadata without a checkout (git init, the project's object store as an alternate, update-ref to the snapshot, read-tree), so that HEAD is the snapshot and rule H4 judges the handoffs as committed, as on the runner; a copy whose HEAD is not the snapshot would see every handoff as 'not in a commit' and let a PENDING one pass. Proposal for ORCH: write the way the copy gets its git metadata into AP-141 (item 2) and into the task text of the next snapshot step.

My first push attempt was refused by git on this machine ('src refspec … does not match any') because zsh treats ':r' right after a variable as a modifier: "$SHA:refs/heads/…" lost its tail. Nothing reached GitHub (ls-remote right after: only main), and no run was started by it. The second attempt with the variable in braces worked. A lesson that can repeat for any step that pushes a <sha>:<ref> refspec from a variable in zsh; ORCH decides whether it goes into the error journal.

One npm run check leaves 203 new sai-* entries in the system temporary root (195 sai-wf06-, 5 sai-outside-, 2 sai-snap-, 1 sai-flaky-), the same as at step 05h; they come from test files outside this work (step 05, I11), not from the e2e kit (0 sai-e2e-). I left them in place. ORCH decides whether a defect is needed or already open.

This GitHub run took 376 s, the test step 296 s. The earlier GitHub runs of the full check took 836 s (run 41678354227) and 17 min 00 s (run 41701454358), both on 2026-11-03 with 2185 and 2187 tests. Why this one was shorter is not established: it is one sample, on image version 20261111.370.1. The runner used Chrome/157.0.8103.50; this Mac used Chrome/157.0.8103.78.
